html:
Roman reformer who was tribune of the plebs in 123 and 122 BCE, ten years after his brother Tiberius Gracchus was killed.

He pushed a much wider program than his brother:

  • revived the land law and its commission;
  • sold grain to citizens at a low fixed price, the start of the Roman grain dole;
  • founded colonies, one of them on the site of Carthage;
  • built roads and granaries;
  • took the extortion courts from senators and gave them to juries of equites, the rich class outside the Senate.

His proposal to give Roman citizenship to Rome's Latin allies failed, and he lost support. In 121 BCE the Senate passed its first "final decree", telling the consul Lucius Opimius to protect the state. Opimius attacked Gaius and his followers on the Aventine Hill. Gaius had a slave kill him, and thousands of his supporters were later put to death.

The question of the allies he raised led thirty years later to the Social War.
sum: Roman reformer who was tribune of the plebs in 123 and 122 BCE, ten years after his brother Tiberius Gracchus was killed.
